problem: Bluetooth headset: low-quality/call-like audio in match or no voice chat (HFP/A2DP switch)
symptoms: In-game volume very low or call-quality once voice chat starts in a match
After disabling Hands-Free Telephony, game audio is fine but teammates cannot be heard (voice icons show activity)
Game detects output but not input device on Bluetooth headset (AirPods, Sony WH-CH520, Realme Buds)
root_causes: Windows switches Bluetooth headset from Stereo (A2DP) to Hands-Free (HFP/HSP) profile when Valorant opens the mic for voice chat

fixes.fix: Launch Valorant with party/voice chat on (quality will be bad, keep it). Windows Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Devices > More devices and printer settings > right-click headset > Properties > Services tab > uncheck 'Hands-Free Telephony'. Disconnect headset from PC (do not power it off), reconnect, repeat the uncheck step again, then turn the Bluetooth device off and on. Desktop audio may vanish after first uncheck; repeating after reconnect restores it.

diagnostic_signals: Bluetooth audio device present as default playback/recording device
Bluetooth device services: HandsFree Telephony enabled
Default device vs Default Communication device mismatch in Sound control panel

problem: Stutter / FPS drops / lag spikes caused by Realtek 2.5GbE network adapter (Windows + Vanguard/UE5)
symptoms: Micro-stutters or freezes every 2-15 seconds, FPS drops from hundreds to 1-10 for a fraction of a second
Only Valorant affected (other games fine), CPU/GPU render latency spikes
Started after new PC build or the 17 Feb patch; also seen on Fortnite
Stutter occurs even when playing on Wi-Fi if the onboard Realtek 2.5GbE adapter is enabled
root_causes: Realtek Gaming/PCIe 2.5GbE Family Controller driver and its power-saving features (EEE, Green Ethernet, Windows sleep interaction) interfering with Vanguard/game, typically on B650/B850 AMD boards

fixes.fix: Device Manager > Network adapters > right-click 'Realtek Gaming 2.5GbE Family Controller' (or Realtek PCIe 2.5GbE) > Disable (not uninstall). Use Wi-Fi or another NIC meanwhile. Re-enable if it does not help.

To keep using Ethernet: install the Realtek 'Not Support Power Saving' auto-installer (NDIS / netadapter CX for Win11) or an older driver such as 9.1.410.2015 (9.4 also mentioned); in adapter Properties > Power Management untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'; Advanced tab disable Energy-Efficient Ethernet, Flow Control, Gigabit Lite, Green Ethernet, Interrupt Moderation, Power Saving Mode. Also take driver from motherboard vendor.
Switching from Wi-Fi to Ethernet cable (user on a board with Realtek 2.5GbE) removed the stutters.
Disable the Wi-Fi adapter instead if on wired and stutter persists.
Wired-in Wi-Fi booster/extender was the trigger in one case; unplugging it let the 2.5GbE adapter work without lag.

diagnostic_signals: Presence of Realtek 2.5GbE adapter in Get-NetAdapter / driver name and version
Adapter power management 'allow computer to turn off device' enabled
Adapter advanced properties: EEE/Green Ethernet/Interrupt Moderation values
Valorant render latency vs network (correlated CPU/GPU latency spikes)

problem: Packet loss / network jitter on Wi-Fi, router or ISP routing
symptoms: Packet loss indicator climbing in match (1-20%, sometimes hundreds/thousands of packets) while other games fine
Ping spikes in gunfights
Packet loss only on specific servers (Paris/London, Mumbai/Singapore)
root_causes: Wi-Fi interference/unreliable routing
ISP routing/IP problem after router replacement
NIC buffer settings mismatch (claimed)
Electrical noise from PC/monitor power strip near router (claimed, unverified)
Unstable CPU overclock (suggested)

fixes.fix: Switch from Wi-Fi to Ethernet cable.
Contact ISP to refresh routing/IP (fixed packet loss with new Wi-Fi 6 router; ping 6-7ms).
Device Manager > network adapter > Properties > Advanced: set Receive Buffers to 2x Transmit Buffers (guide author reports fix on several PCs; limited by driver max).
Router on its own wall outlet, power strip with PC/monitor ~0.5 m away; do not set MTU too low (e.g. 1280) - tune MTU only up to real path limit.
Cloudflare WARP (1.1.1.1) while playing - helped one user with packet loss on Paris/London but did not fully solve.
Cap FPS, run bufferbloat test and enable QoS/SQM, turn off multithreaded rendering, check CPU overclock stability.

diagnostic_signals: Packet loss/jitter to Riot servers (ping test/pingplotter)
MTU value (netsh interface ipv4 show subinterfaces)

problem: High ping due to ISP routing change (ACT Fibernet India, NA Georgia/Virginia)
symptoms: Ping jumped (e.g. 13 to 54-60ms, or 25 to 60ms) suddenly for one ISP/region
Other regional servers unaffected
root_causes: ISP re-routing traffic through a distant hub (e.g. Delhi then Mumbai), or upstream/Cloudflare routing issue; often resolves itself

fixes.fix: Use Cloudflare WARP (1.1.1.1) while gaming; ping dropped from ~55 to 16 ms for ACT users.
ExitLag restored ping from ~58 to ~39 ms.
Wait; issue resolved by itself in some cases. Riot support suggested public DNS and disabling VPN (did not help).

diagnostic_signals: Ping to each Riot server/region and traceroute hops

problem: Ping spikes every few seconds after patch - fixed by Vanguard reinstall
symptoms: Ping spikes every 3-4 seconds on wired connection after new patch
Micro-stutter after patch
root_causes: Corrupted/mismatched Vanguard install after update (unconfirmed)

fixes.fix: Reinstall Riot Vanguard (OP had to reinstall Riot Client and Valorant too because Vanguard reinstall alone failed).

diagnostic_signals: Vanguard version vs Riot client version

problem: VAN: Incompatible software component detected (ene.sys RGB driver / se64a.sys monitor driver)
symptoms: Vanguard popup 'incompatible software component' on every launch naming C:\Windows\System32\drivers\ene.sys or se64a.sys
Game will not start; Vanguard flags driver as cheat vector
root_causes: ene.sys: old ENE RGB controller driver bundled with RGB software (RGB Fusion, Asus Aura, MSI Dragon Center, Razer Synapse 3)
se64a.sys: old EnTech Taiwan monitor-control driver from Monitor Asset Manager / softOSD (Dell), CVE-2023-2870

fixes.fix: Update/replace the RGB software (Razer Synapse 4, motherboard vendor tool) or uninstall it (e.g. Asus Aura).
Rename C:\Windows\System32\drivers\ene.sys to ene.sys.old (or .bak); if locked, boot Safe Mode (Shift+Restart) and rename/delete, then restart. One user then got VAN 84 instead.
Uninstall Monitor Asset Manager / softOSD, reboot, delete C:\Windows\System32\drivers\se64a.sys; if undeletable run 'sc delete se64a' in admin cmd, reboot, then delete.

diagnostic_signals: Installed RGB/monitor control software (RGB Fusion, Aura, Dragon Center, Synapse, Monitor Asset Manager, softOSD)
Registered kernel driver services ene / se64a (sc query)

problem: Vanguard restriction: Memory Integrity (HVCI) / virtualization required - crash, 'HVCI enabled' or VAN 185
symptoms: PC hard shuts off (Kernel-Power 41) shortly after pressing Play with no BSOD
Vanguard message 'HVCI enabled' / does not meet requirements
Memory Integrity toggle reverts to off after reboot or says incompatible driver
VAN 185 persisting after everything else tried
root_causes: Vanguard now requires Memory Integrity/core isolation on; needs CPU virtualization (Intel VT-x / AMD SVM) and Secure Boot/UEFI
Incompatible driver blocks enabling Memory Integrity (e.g. xhunter1.sys from XIGNCODE3 anti-cheat of another game)

fixes.fix: Enable CPU virtualization in BIOS (SVM Mode / Intel VT-x), ensure Secure Boot + UEFI, then Windows Security > Core isolation > Memory integrity ON. Crash-on-launch fixed for OP.
When Memory Integrity shows incompatible driver, find it in the list (xhunter1.sys) and remove the offending anti-cheat/software (PUBG/XIGNCODE3), then enable.
Third-party PowerShell script automating HVCI enable via Device Guard registry (unverified).
For VAN 185: turning core isolation on then off (HVCI restriction shown) and not playing ~2 days, error gone for 2 months (author speculates account reset; risky).
Update BIOS; read Riot 'Vanguard Restrictions' article and enable all listed BIOS/Windows items.

diagnostic_signals: CPU virtualization enabled (systeminfo / Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor VirtualizationFirmwareEnabled)

problem: Secure Boot / UEFI / TPM requirement not met on older or misconfigured boards (VAN 9003, VAN 9090 TPM failure)
symptoms: 'Need UEFI Secure Boot' message after working before
Secure Boot option greyed/hidden in BIOS
Crash with VAN9003 on new PC
VAN 9090 TPM failure while playing
root_causes: CSM/Legacy mode enabled, Secure Boot keys not installed, fTPM disabled in BIOS; options hidden in Advanced menus on old MSI boards

fixes.fix: In BIOS: disable CSM, save/restart, then Secure Boot option appears; enable it, set mode to Custom > 'Restore Factory Keys', save and restart; verify in msinfo32 (Secure Boot State On).

Old MSI B250M board: check disk is GPT (diskpart > list disk, asterisk in GPT column), UEFI only (not UEFI+Legacy), enable TPM/fTPM; Secure Boot keys/Fast Boot options were hidden under Advanced options - OP solved it by finding them.
Enable fTPM and Secure Boot in BIOS (fixed VAN9003 crash).
Update BIOS to latest; confirm UEFI mode and Secure Boot actually on (a user had never enabled UEFI/Secure Boot).

diagnostic_signals: Disk partition style GPT vs MBR (Get-Disk)

problem: VAN 9101 attestation failure (security violation #0000002) after Feb patch
symptoms: Error repeats every 3-5 minutes and closes client despite TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot on
Started suddenly after a game/Windows update; reported mostly on AMD systems and Windows 11 26H1 / Insider builds
root_causes: Unknown; thread suggests Vanguard update or Windows 11 26H1/Insider build interaction; Intel rig of same user worked
diagnostic_signals: TPM type (fTPM AMD vs Intel PTT)

problem: IOMMU must be enabled / account not meeting criteria (Vanguard + Win11 24H2/25H2)
symptoms: Vanguard says IOMMU must be enabled although VT-d/DMA protection/VBS/HVCI all active
DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL BSOD; vgc.exe crash BEX64 c0000409
Short temporary suspensions
root_causes: Vanguard IOMMU detection not matching newer OEM laptops (HP Victus locked BIOS) - unconfirmed

fixes.fix: Uninstall Valorant/vgc/vgk; tpm.msc > Clear TPM, reboot; toggle Memory Integrity off, reboot, on again; enable Kernel-mode Hardware-enforced Stack Protection; reinstall Valorant via Epic Games launcher (one commenter's fix).
Wait for Vanguard update or OEM BIOS exposing IOMMU; OP uninstalled game and never confirmed a fix.

diagnostic_signals: IOMMU/DMA protection status (msinfo32 Kernel DMA Protection)

problem: Vanguard BSOD / game requires restart loop - broken Vanguard install
symptoms: BSOD when launching Valorant; 'Your game requires a system restart to play' even after restart
VAN 1067 / VAN -1
BSOD when uninstalling Valorant (vgk.sys)
Straight crash or BSOD from vgk.sys that persists after reinstall
root_causes: Corrupted Vanguard drivers/services (vgk, vgc)
Possible deeper OS-level issue when nothing else works

fixes.fix: Admin cmd: 'sc delete vgk' and 'sc delete vgc', restart, download Vanguard setup.exe (1.17.18.4 from riotcdn) and run as admin, launch Valorant, restart again if prompted.
Boot from installer USB and delete ALL disk partitions during Windows install (a plain Windows reset did not fix VAN 1067/-1).
After BSOD on uninstall, just remove Riot Vanguard too.
Check BIOS settings/UEFI + Secure Boot; update BIOS and GPU driver.

diagnostic_signals: vgk/vgc service state (sc query vgk, vgc)
Minidump / BSOD stop code and faulting module vgk.sys

problem: Valorant fails to launch ('Something unusual happened' / nothing happens)
symptoms: Riot client opens but Valorant failed to launch; or Valorant shows in taskbar grey and desktop freezes when clicked
Vanguard won't start despite reinstall
root_causes: Registry/Windows security changes (cracked software modified registry value)
Launch path via client broken
Vanguard restrictions requirements not met
Possible Windows corruption

fixes.fix: Launch with shortcut: "C:\Riot Games\Riot Client\RiotClientServices.exe" --launch-product=valorant --launch-patchline=live, run as administrator (adjust drive).
Cracked Vegas editing software had modified a registry value; after fixing it Valorant launched.
Satisfy Vanguard Restrictions article (BIOS/Windows items); OP changed several things and it worked.
Set DWORD DevOverrideEnable = 0 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options, restart.
msconfig > Services > hide Microsoft services, disable all others, keep vgc on (temporary workaround).
Reset PC / reinstall Windows via cloud install (worked for OP); delete all Riot folders including mods.

diagnostic_signals: Image File Execution Options entries (DevOverrideEnable, debugger hooks)
Third-party software modifying registry/Windows Smart App Control state

problem: Stuck on loading screen / VAL 43
symptoms: Riot client fine but Valorant loading bar stuck at ~5% or blue cursor forever
VAL 43 sometimes
root_causes: Windows Firewall blocking (one case)
Third-party apps such as National Instruments or Bonjour interfering (suggested); leftover 360 Total Security network drivers (suspected)

fixes.fix: Turn off Windows Firewall (reported fix).
Check DxDiag logs for National Instruments / Bonjour software and remove.

diagnostic_signals: Installed software: National Instruments, Bonjour, 360 Total Security

problem: Fatal/blank error after update - clean reinstall of Riot files
symptoms: Fatal error right after 165 MB update
Blank (no-code) error popup
Long-running desync/odd behavior despite reinstalls
Update loops back to 'Update' button
root_causes: Corrupted leftover files/settings in Riot folders

fixes.fix: Full clean reinstall: delete C:\Riot Games\Riot Client, delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\Riot Games and %PROGRAMDATA%\Riot Games, empty recycle bin, remove Vanguard and Valorant with Revo Uninstaller, then reinstall (Riot support recipe).
Reinstall after fatal error post-update.
Deleting Riot Games folders in AppData and ProgramData noticeably improved desync/hit registration.

problem: Stuck/auto-firing or non-working inputs after patch (left click, ADS, reload) - corrupt config
symptoms: Left click fires continuously, only ESC stops it
Right click stuck in ADS/hold
Cannot reload after first reload, key must be rebound each round
Mouse won't move/click in tutorial
root_causes: Corrupted VALORANT settings/config files after patch; conflicting keybind (Ghost mode)

fixes.fix: Close game and client; delete all files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\VALORANT\Saved\Config (delete again if they reappear); start custom game 5 min; Settings > Controls > Reset to game defaults (Riot support steps).
Delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\VALORANT\Saved folder (backup crosshairs first).
Unbind Ghost mode / conflicting keybind (fixed can't-reload bug).
Toggle Raw Input Buffer setting / mouse properties tweak for mouse that won't move in tutorial.

problem: Mouse fast-movement lag / stutter from USB port or driver
symptoms: Camera does not follow fast flicks, jitter; micro-stutters after clean install
Mouse input delayed or ignored
root_causes: Mouse on USB 2.0 port instead of 3.0 (one case)
New NVIDIA driver (suggested)
High polling rate CPU load (suggested)

fixes.fix: Move mouse to a USB 3.0 port.
DDU and roll back NVIDIA driver to 581.80; turn off enhance pointer precision; set polling to 500-1000Hz.

problem: Valorant has no audio or voice chat broken (output device / ExitLag / exclusive mode / USB power saving)
symptoms: No game audio only in Valorant after PC rebuild
Mic dies mid-game / system-wide
Voice chat icons vanish and push-to-talk dies when ExitLag on
USB interface mic disconnects mid-match
root_causes: Valorant assigned to wrong output in Windows per-app volume
Applications taking exclusive control of mic
ExitLag dual-routing / redirect-login options
USB audio interface power saving

fixes.fix: Win+I > System > Sound > Advanced > App volume and device preferences: check output device used by Valorant.
Turn off ExitLag 'dual routing' option (and possibly redirect login).
Control Panel > Sound > Recording > mic > Properties > Advanced: untick 'Allow applications to take exclusive control'.
Device Manager > devices by container > USB Input Device > Power Management: untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device'; set format 1ch 16/24-bit 48000Hz (did not solve for OP).

problem: Game freezes or crashes on click/lobby (display mode, user profile, third-party freezes)
symptoms: Freezes upon clicking any button
Freezes 10s per action; crashes when shooting
Freeze 5-10s when using chat or Alt+Tab
PC freezes ~1 minute after opening game
root_causes: Display mode not set to fullscreen/windowed
Corrupted Windows user profile
Bluetooth software hook btmmhook.dll
iGPU disabled in BIOS on a Ryzen with dedicated GPU

fixes.fix: Press F11 to set display mode to fullscreen/windowed.
Log in with a different Windows user account.
Uninstall old Bluetooth software (btmmhook.dll hook visible in Task Manager error); or rename btmmhook.dll in System32 to .old.
Enable iGPU in BIOS (7600X): freeze ended even when playing on dedicated GPU.

problem: PC hard freeze or reboot a few minutes after launching Valorant (unresolved / Defender)
symptoms: Entire PC hangs and needs hard reset in lobby after 2-4 min, blue circle cursor then crash
Freeze during queue/agent select
Happens only in Valorant
root_causes: Unknown; suggestions include real-time protection / run as admin, BIOS update, Windows repair-reinstall, GPU driver issues on Radeon 9060 XT

fixes.fix: Disable Windows Defender real-time protection and run via desktop shortcut as administrator (OP believes it fixed freeze, unconfirmed long term).
Repair-reinstall Windows keeping apps and files (Settings > System > Recovery > Fix problems using Windows Update) - worked for commenter.
Rename Valorant and Riot Client folders in AppData\Local to .OLD; update BIOS; set vgc service to Automatic.

diagnostic_signals: Event log Kernel-Power 41 and Event Viewer critical errors

problem: Third-party antivirus / security software conflicts with Vanguard (VAL 5, VAN 102, lag)
symptoms: VAN -102 asking to restart client, then VAL 5 after a few rounds with temp bans
Lag in Valorant only
root_causes: Trend Micro blocking Vanguard/Riot files; other third-party AV (Norton etc.)

fixes.fix: Add exceptions in Trend Micro for ~6 files (3 Vanguard files, Riot Games folder, 2 Valorant files) - fixed after Riot staff log review.
Uninstall third-party antivirus (e.g. Norton) leaving Windows Defender (with Realtek fix).
Add vgc to Windows Defender exceptions.

diagnostic_signals: Installed AV products (Trend Micro, Norton, 360 Total Security)

problem: VAL 57 / VAL 59 connection errors
symptoms: VAL 57 or 59 on opening game after patch; codes alternate
root_causes: IPv6 handling on adapter (claimed)
Killer Intelligence Center network optimisation (claimed)

fixes.fix: After reinstalling Vanguard, uncheck Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6) in Ethernet adapter Properties.
Disable features in Killer Intelligence Center and update Intel drivers.
Uninstall only Vanguard from Add/Remove Programs, reopen Riot client to reinstall, restart (did not fix OP).

problem: VAL 29 after installing FACEIT
symptoms: VAL 29 when launching Valorant right after installing FACEIT anticheat
root_causes: Conflict between FACEIT anti-cheat and Vanguard

fixes.fix: Restart whole PC (worked for OP, who had also uninstalled FACEIT).
Uninstall FACEIT and Vanguard, reinstall FACEIT then Vanguard.

problem: Frame-time/latency spikes (Game Latency CPU, Render Latency GPU, chat delay)
symptoms: FPS falls from 600-1000 to 80-200 after update
Game latency CPU/GPU spikes, text chat 1s delay
Stutters when much action
root_causes: Packet loss/jitter making engine wait for packets (Riot support)
NVIDIA driver regression (suggested)
Discord running in background

fixes.fix: Fresh Windows install fixed it for OP.
Roll back NVIDIA driver to early-2025 version with DDU.
Add vgc to Defender exceptions; run Revo Uninstaller then reinstall; start vgc service before game.
Close Discord or set its priority to lowest in Task Manager (helped some).

problem: Low FPS from power mode, throttling, storage or RAM
symptoms: Valorant 60-80 FPS with CPU below 2GHz on laptop
FPS fell after update on laptop iGPU
Slow loading, stuck at agent select with game on external HDD and 8GB RAM
Low VRAM use after clean install of laptop
root_causes: Laptop on efficiency/power-saver profile
Throttling
Game on HDD / insufficient RAM
Laptop stuck in quiet/limp mode (Lenovo Vantage not installable during Microsoft outage)

fixes.fix: Set Windows power mode to best performance when plugged in.
Install game on SSD, upgrade RAM above 8GB; disable background apps and enable Game Mode.
Issue resolved after Microsoft Store outage ended and Lenovo Vantage could be installed (laptop performance mode).

diagnostic_signals: CPU clock vs max and throttling
Valorant install drive type (HDD vs SSD)

problem: Tearing/choppiness or blur with G-Sync/V-Sync
symptoms: Blur when vsync off at 300-450 fps
Choppy/jittery at high fps with tearing on external 180Hz monitor
'D-sub out of range' black screen after first launch
root_causes: G-Sync/V-Sync interaction and fps cap mismatch
Refresh rate/resolution out of range for monitor

fixes.fix: Turn off G-Sync in NVIDIA Control Panel.
G-Sync + V-Sync ON in NVCP and cap FPS to just below monitor refresh (e.g. 171 for 180Hz).
Alt+Enter to windowed to set resolution/refresh; delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\VALORANT\Saved\Config.

diagnostic_signals: Monitor refresh rate vs game setting

problem: Valorant on PlayStation (PS5/Portal) cannot connect
symptoms: PS5 disconnects from servers / slow to menu for a week, mainly Germany
Many error codes on PlayStation Portal
root_causes: Account/connection state tied to console; Portal/remote play blocked for Valorant

fixes.fix: Have a friend log into Valorant with your PSN account from their console, then log back in at home.
PS5 Wi-Fi band to 5 GHz only and set manual DNS 8.8.8.8 / 8.8.4.4.
Portal/Remote Play is blocked by Riot (no fix).

problem: Account login / MFA / matchmaking glitches (non-technical)
symptoms: MFA code emailed to a stranger's address
Agent select dodging bug for everyone
Account appears offline
root_causes: Account data error or Riot server-side bug

fixes.fix: Email Riot support to correct MFA email.
Server bug fixed by Riot itself.
